sections.title: 1. Agile Methodology & Persona Mapping
sections.body:
This document outlines the Agile user stories for the Hospital Management System (HMS), structured to support iterative development and continuous delivery. The system is designed to provide a centralized platform for managing hospital operations, patient information, medical records, appointments, and administrative functions. 

**Personas:**
- **Admin**: Oversees system configuration, user management, and high-level reporting.
- **Doctor**: Manages patient consultations, diagnoses, prescriptions, and clinical notes.
- **Nurse**: Handles patient care, vital signs, nursing notes, and bed management.
- **Receptionist**: Manages patient registration, appointment scheduling, and queue management.
- **Pharmacist**: Manages pharmacy prescriptions, medicine inventory, and dispensing.
- **Lab Technician**: Processes laboratory test requests and generates reports.
- **Accountant**: Manages billing, payments, insurance, invoices, and hospital expenses.
- **Patient**: Views appointments, prescriptions, reports, bills, and medical history via a portal.

**Methodology:**
- User stories are organized into Epics based on core functional modules.
- Each story follows the format: *As a [Persona], I want [Capability] so that [Business Value].*
- Priorities are assigned based on criticality to hospital operations and compliance requirements (e.g., HIPAA, GDPR).

sections.title: 3. Release Slicing & Implementation Dependencies
sections.body:
**Release Slicing:**
- **Release 1 (MVP):** Authentication, Patient Management, Appointment Scheduling, EMR, and Billing. These modules form the core operational backbone of the HMS.
- **Release 2:** Laboratory Management, Pharmacy Management, and Notifications. These modules enhance clinical workflows and patient engagement.
- **Release 3:** Inventory & Procurement, Reports & Analytics, and Advanced Audit Features. These modules support administrative efficiency and compliance.

**Implementation Dependencies:**
- **Authentication & Access Control** must be implemented first, as all other modules depend on secure user access.
- **Patient Management** is a prerequisite for Appointment Scheduling, EMR, and Billing.
- **EMR** is a prerequisite for Laboratory Management and Pharmacy Management, as these modules rely on patient clinical data.
- **Billing** depends on Appointment Scheduling, EMR, and Laboratory/Pharmacy Management for accurate invoice generation.
- **Audit & Compliance** features must be integrated across all modules to ensure end-to-end traceability and regulatory compliance.

File: A Hospital Management System.pdf
--- Page 1 ---
Hospital Management System 
A Hospital Management System (HMS)  should provide a centralized platform for 
managing hospital operations, patient information, medical records, appointments, doctors, 
nurses, staff, billing, pharmacy, laboratory, and inventory. The system should support  role-
based access  for Admin, Doctor, Nurse, Receptionist, Pharmacist, Lab Technician, 
Accountant, and Patient. Core requirements should include patient registration and profile 
management, appointment scheduling and queue management, doctor availability, O PD/IPD 
management, admission/discharge/transfer, electronic medical records, diagnosis, 
prescriptions, treatment history, allergies, vital signs, nursing notes, laboratory test requests 
and reports, pharmacy prescriptions and medicine inventory, bed/ward m anagement, billing 
and payments, insurance management, invoices and receipts, hospital expenses, staff 
management, and inventory/procurement. Patients should be able to view appointments, 
prescriptions, reports, bills, and medical history through a portal,  while doctors should have 
dashboards for appointments, patient records, diagnosis, prescriptions, and clinical notes. 
The system should also provide  dashboards, notifications, search/filtering, reports, audit 
logs, data validation, backup/recovery, security, and role -based authorization . 
Functional requirements should cover complete workflows such as  patient registration → 
appointment → consultation → diagnosis → laboratory/pharmacy → billing → follow -
up, and admission → bed allocation → treatment → investigations → discharge → final 
billing. Non -functional requirements should include responsive web UI, scalability, high 
availability, fast API responses , secure authentication, password encryption, session 
management, HTTPS, database integrity, auditability, privacy of medical information, error 
handling, logging, and regular backups. A suitable architecture can use  React/Next.js for 
frontend, FastAPI/Node.js/Spring Boot for backend, PostgreSQL/MySQL for database, 
REST APIs, JWT/OAuth-based authentication, Redis for caching/queues, and cloud or 
on-premise deployment , with separate modules for  Authentication, Patients, 
Appointments, EMR, Doctors, Nursing, L aboratory, Pharmacy, Billing, Inventory, 
Staff, Reports, Notifications, and Administration.
